3285	    @staticmethod
3286	    def _evaluate_inspection_rows(
3287	        meta_rows: tuple,
3288	        event_rows: tuple,
3289	        anchor_rows: tuple,
3290	        request_rows: tuple,
3291	        generation_rows: tuple,
3292	        secret: str | None,
3293	        history_secrets: Mapping[int, str],
3294	        scope: tuple[str, str],
3295	    ) -> list[str]:
3296	        """Pure, read-only per-request evaluation of the persisted chain.
3297	
3298	        Kept free of any connection so the logic is deterministic and
3299	        side-effect free: it only compares and recomputes, never writes.
3300	        Returns the sorted stable reason codes that make the scoped
3301	        request's settled audit chain untrusted -- an empty list means
3302	        the request verifies. Two layers are assessed:
3303	
3304	        * the request's own evidence: event order and database link
3305	          hashes, the request row's chain head and current status, the
3306	          one-to-one event/anchor binding and every anchor's
3307	          authentication under the secret of the generation recorded on
3308	          its own row;
3309	        * the file-wide seal the request cannot be trusted without: the
3310	          singleton meta head, the secret-generation records, the
3311	          gap-free global commit order, the replayed global anchor head
3312	          and file-wide split or orphaned evidence.
3313	        """
3314	        scope_tenant, scope_request = scope
3315	        global_reasons: set[str] = set()
3316	        scoped_reasons: set[str] = set()
3317	
3318	        # -- singleton meta head (file-wide) -------------------------
3319	        stored_head: str | None = None
3320	        if len(meta_rows) > 1:
3321	            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_META_CORRUPT)
3322	        elif meta_rows:
3323	            stored_head = meta_rows[0][0]
3324	            if not _is_chain_hash(stored_head):
3325	                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_META_CORRUPT)
3326	                stored_head = None
3327	
3328	        # -- secret generations (file-wide) --------------------------
3329	        # One gap-free row per generation that has ever sealed anchors,
3330	        # starting at 1, each with a well-formed fingerprint and an
3331	        # effective time; legacy anchors carry NULL and are attributed
3332	        # to generation 1.
3333	        generation_fingerprints: dict[int, str] = {}
3334	        generation_corrupt = False
3335	        for index, grow in enumerate(generation_rows, start=1):
3336	            generation, fingerprint, effective_at = grow
3337	            if (
3338	                not isinstance(generation, int)
3339	                or isinstance(generation, bool)
3340	                or generation != index
3341	                or not _is_chain_hash(fingerprint)
3342	                or not isinstance(effective_at, str)
3343	                or not _RFC3339_RE.match(effective_at)
3344	            ):
3345	                generation_corrupt = True
3346	            if isinstance(generation, int) and not isinstance(generation, bool):
3347	                generation_fingerprints[generation] = fingerprint
3348	        if anchor_rows and generation_corrupt:
3349	            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_CORRUPT_ROW)

3351	            # Secret generations without a single anchor are only valid
3352	            # as the bootstrap-rotation shape (exactly generations 1 and
3353	            # 2 sharing one effective time).
3354	            bootstrap_shape = (
3355	                not generation_corrupt
3356	                and [g for g, _f, _t in generation_rows] == [1, 2]
3357	                and generation_rows[0][2] == generation_rows[1][2]
3358	            )
3359	            if not bootstrap_shape:
3360	                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_CORRUPT_ROW)
3361	
3362	        # -- event/anchor population invariants (file-wide) ----------
3363	        # A database with events but no anchor rows is the historical
3364	        # un-anchored shape: old content is never judged trusted.
3365	        legacy_unanchored = bool(event_rows) and not anchor_rows
3366	        if legacy_unanchored:
3367	            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_UNANCHORED)
3368	        if anchor_rows and not event_rows:
3369	            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_STATE_SPLIT)
3370	        if anchor_rows and stored_head is None:
3371	            # Sealed anchors without a global head: an interrupted
3372	            # commit or out-of-band deletion.
3373	            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_META_CORRUPT)
3374	
3375	        # -- index the rows ------------------------------------------

3377	        # request's seal is replayed against, so it is a file-wide
3378	        # reason rather than a per-request one.
3379	        events: dict[tuple, tuple] = {}
3380	        for row in event_rows:
3381	            tenant_id, request_id, seq, status, occurred_at, chain_hash = row
3382	            key = (tenant_id, request_id, seq)
3383	            if (
3384	                not isinstance(tenant_id, str)
3385	                or not tenant_id
3386	                or not isinstance(request_id, str)
3387	                or not request_id
3388	                or not isinstance(seq, int)
3389	                or isinstance(seq, bool)
3390	                or not isinstance(status, str)
3391	                or not status
3392	                or not isinstance(occurred_at, str)
3393	                or not occurred_at
3394	                or not _is_chain_hash(chain_hash)
3395	            ):
3396	                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_CORRUPT_ROW)

3398	                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_CORRUPT_ROW)

3400	
3401	        anchors: dict[tuple, tuple] = {}
3402	        for row in anchor_rows:
3403	            (
3404	                commit_seq,
3405	                tenant_id,
3406	                request_id,
3407	                seq,
3408	                event_hash,
3409	                anchor_hmac,

3418	                or not tenant_id
3419	                or not isinstance(request_id, str)
3420	                or not request_id

3434	                )
3435	            ):

3449	        for tenant_id, request_id, _seq in list(events) + list(anchors):

3451	                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_ASSOCIATION)
3452	
3453	        # -- the scoped request's own chain --------------------------
3454	        scope_key = (scope_tenant, scope_request)
3455	        scoped_event_keys = {
3456	            key for key in events if (key[0], key[1]) == scope_key
3457	        }
3458	        scoped_anchor_keys = {
3459	            key for key in anchors if (key[0], key[1]) == scope_key
3460	        }
3461	        # One-to-one binding: every event anchored, every anchor an
3462	        # event. A legacy database with no anchors at all is already
3463	        # reported as the single unanchored reason and must not cascade.
3464	        if not legacy_unanchored and scoped_event_keys - scoped_anchor_keys:
3465	            scoped_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_EVENT_UNANCHORED)
3466	        if scoped_anchor_keys - scoped_event_keys:
3467	            scoped_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_ANCHOR_ORPHAN)

    # -- read-only audit inspection ------------------------------------

    def audit_inspection(
        self,
        tenant_id: str,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        limit: int | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Inspect a tenant's settled audit chains in resumable batches.

        Storage-layer only; never routed over HTTP. With ``cursor``
        omitted a new persistent batch sweeps the tenant's requests in
        stable acceptance order (``created_at`` then ``request_id``);
        with a cursor the batch it names is resumed from its durably
        committed position, so a retry after an interruption or a
        service restart continues instead of restarting, and the same
        cursor always keeps the same batch identifier. Each call
        inspects at most ``limit`` requests (default 100, at most 1000)
        and returns exactly ``batch_id``, ``next_cursor`` (``None`` once
        the sweep is finished), ``finished`` and ``items`` -- one
        ``{"request_id", "verified", "reason"}`` entry per scanned
        request, in scan order. ``verified`` is a boolean and
        ``reason`` the stable, detail-free reason code the request's
        chain failed with (the empty string when it verified).

        Each request is assessed against its settled audit evidence
        exactly like the read-only full-chain verification: the event
        order and database link hashes, the request row's chain head
        and current status, the one-to-one event/anchor binding, every
        anchor's authentication under its own sealing generation, and
        the file-wide seal (the singleton meta head, the secret
        generation records, the gap-free global commit order and the
        replayed global anchor head). A healthy request verifies with
        an empty reason; deleted, altered, inserted or reordered
        events, cross-request or cross-tenant substitutions, a tampered
        chain head, anchor or global head, a missing historical secret,
        a broken generation association, a forged chain, an un-anchored
        legacy database and an interrupted commit all report
        ``verified`` false with a stable reason code.

        The sweep is strictly read-only for every audit, anchor and key
        record: it never repairs, backfills, recomputes or overwrites
        them. Only the inspection bookkeeping tables are written -- the
        batch row, one item row per scanned request and the cursor
        position, each item committing in its own transaction together
        with the position advance, so a failed call never returns
        half-settled results and a committed item is never re-reported.

        A non-string/empty *tenant_id*, a limit outside 1..1000 (or a
        non-integer or boolean), and any malformed, unknown or
        cross-tenant *cursor* raise :class:`ValueError` without
        writing. Corrupt persisted batch state and every storage fault
        raise the fixed-text :class:`OSError`.
        """
        # Validate everything before touching the database: no rejected
        # call may perform a write.
        tenant_id = _require_nonempty_str(tenant_id, "tenant_id")
        if limit is None:
            limit = _DEFAULT_BATCH_LIMIT
        limit = _require_batch_limit(limit)
        cursor_batch: tuple[str, int] | None = None
        if cursor is not None:
            cursor_batch = _decode_cursor(cursor, _INSPECTION_CURSOR_PREFIX)

        with self._write_lock:
            conn = self._connect()
            try:
                # First transaction resolves the batch: a fresh batch row
                # is inserted when no cursor was given; a cursor names the
                # persisted batch to resume. An unknown/cross-tenant cursor
                # is rejected here before anything is written.
                batch_id, _pos, _rid, finished, _start_count = (
                    self._batch_transaction(
                        conn,
                        lambda: self._load_or_init_inspection_locked(
                            conn, tenant_id, cursor_batch
                        ),
                    )
                )
                items: list[dict[str, object]] = []
                # Each scanned request is assessed and recorded in its OWN
                # transaction: the item row and the cursor position commit
                # together. The next iteration re-reads the persisted
                # position, so an item already settled by an earlier commit
                # or a concurrent call is never re-reported.
                while not finished and len(items) < limit:
                    kind, payload = self._batch_transaction(
                        conn,
                        lambda: self._process_one_inspection_item_locked(
                            conn, tenant_id, batch_id
                        ),
                    )
                    if kind == "finished":
                        finished = True
                        break
                    items.append(payload)
                # Resolve the authoritative outcome in one final short
                # transaction: whether the sweep is finished AND the durable
                # settled-item count are both read from the database rather
                # than from this call's in-memory tally, so the issued
                # cursor names a position that matches what is durably
                # committed (another store instance may share the file).
                finished, durable_count = self._batch_transaction(
                    conn,
                    lambda: self._finalize_inspection_if_end_locked(
                        conn, tenant_id, batch_id
                    ),
                )
            finally:
                self._release(conn)
        # The cursor only identifies the persisted batch; its item count is
        # the database-authoritative settled count read in the final
        # transaction.
        next_cursor = (
            None
            if finished
            else _encode_cursor(batch_id, durable_count, _INSPECTION_CURSOR_PREFIX)
        )
        # Log only counts and the stable outcome: no tenant, subject,
        # credential or SQL text ever reaches the log.
        _log.info(
            "audit inspection settled items=%s finished=%s",
            len(items),
            finished,
        )
        return {
            "batch_id": batch_id,
            "next_cursor": next_cursor,
            "finished": finished,
            "items": items,
        }

    def _load_or_init_inspection_locked(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        tenant_id: str,
        cursor_batch: tuple[str, int] | None,
    ) -> tuple[str, str | None, str | None, bool, int]:
        """Resolve the inspection batch for this call in an open write txn.

        Returns ``(batch_id, position_created_at, position_request_id,
        finished, item_count)``. Without a cursor a fresh batch row is
        inserted; with a cursor the persisted batch is resumed from its
        committed position -- the cursor's own position field is only a
        format detail, the database is authoritative. An unknown or
        cross-tenant batch id is an invalid cursor and raises
        :class:`ValueError`; corrupt persisted state raises the
        fixed-text :class:`OSError`.
        """
        if cursor_batch is None:
            batch_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO inspection_batches ("
                "batch_id, tenant_id, position_created_at, "
                "position_request_id, finished"
                ") VALUES (?, ?, NULL, NULL, 0)",
                (batch_id, tenant_id),
            )
            return batch_id, None, None, False, 0
        batch_id, _issued_position = cursor_batch
        # Confirm ownership before reading state: an unknown or
        # cross-tenant batch id is an invalid cursor, indistinguishable
        # from one that never existed.
        owner = conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM inspection_batches WHERE batch_id = ? AND tenant_id = ?",
            (batch_id, tenant_id),
        ).fetchone()
        if owner is None:
            raise ValueError("cursor is not valid")
        pos_created, pos_rid, finished, item_count = (
            self._read_inspection_state_locked(conn, batch_id)
        )
        return batch_id, pos_created, pos_rid, finished, item_count

    def _read_inspection_state_locked(
        self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, batch_id: str
    ) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, bool, int]:
        """Read and strictly validate an inspection batch's position."""
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT position_created_at, position_request_id, finished, "
            "(SELECT count(*) FROM inspection_batch_items i "
            " WHERE i.batch_id = b.batch_id) "
            "FROM inspection_batches b WHERE b.batch_id = ?",
            (batch_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            # The batch this transaction is driving vanished out of band.
            raise _storage_failure()
        pos_created, pos_rid, finished, item_count = row
        if (
            finished not in (0, 1)
            or not isinstance(item_count, int)
            or isinstance(item_count, bool)
        ):
            raise _storage_failure()
        if (pos_created is None) != (pos_rid is None):
            # The keyset position is written atomically; a split pair is
            # out-of-band corruption, never a resumable state.
            raise _storage_failure()
        if pos_created is not None and (
            not isinstance(pos_created, str)
            or not pos_created
            or not isinstance(pos_rid, str)
            or not pos_rid
        ):
            raise _storage_failure()
        return pos_created, pos_rid, bool(finished), item_count

    def _process_one_inspection_item_locked(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        tenant_id: str,
        batch_id: str,
    ) -> tuple[str, object]:
        """Inspect the next request in scan order inside an open write txn.

        Re-reads the batch's persisted position every call, so the
        result is independent of any in-memory position. Returns
        ``("finished", None)`` once the sweep end is reached, or
        ``("item", {"request_id", "verified", "reason"})`` after
        assessing one request and recording its item. The request's
        audit evidence is only read: the assessment never repairs,
        backfills, recomputes or overwrites any audit, anchor or key
        record -- the item row and the batch position are the only
        writes, and they commit together.
        """
        pos_created, pos_rid, finished, item_count = (
            self._read_inspection_state_locked(conn, batch_id)
        )
        if finished:
            return "finished", None
        row = self._next_inspection_candidate(conn, tenant_id, pos_created, pos_rid)
        if row is None:
            self._finish_inspection_locked(conn, batch_id)
            return "finished", None
        request_id, created_at = row
        item = self._inspect_request_locked(conn, tenant_id, request_id)
        # The item row and the cursor position land in this one
        # transaction; the sequence derives from the persisted count so
        # a resumed batch never reuses a number.
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO inspection_batch_items ("
            "batch_id, seq, request_id, verified, reason"
            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (
                batch_id,
                item_count + 1,
                request_id,
                1 if item["verified"] else 0,
                item["reason"],
            ),
        )
        self._advance_inspection_locked(conn, batch_id, created_at, request_id)
        return "item", item

    def _finalize_inspection_if_end_locked(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        tenant_id: str,
        batch_id: str,
    ) -> tuple[bool, int]:
        """Finish a limit-stopped inspection iff no candidate remains.

        Always returns the authoritative ``(finished, item_count)`` read
        from the persisted batch inside this write transaction, so the
        caller can issue a cursor whose position matches the durable
        tally rather than its own per-call snapshot.
        """
        pos_created, pos_rid, finished, item_count = (
            self._read_inspection_state_locked(conn, batch_id)
        )
        if finished:
            return True, item_count
        if self._next_inspection_candidate(conn, tenant_id, pos_created, pos_rid) is None:
            self._finish_inspection_locked(conn, batch_id)
            return True, item_count
        return False, item_count

    @staticmethod
    def _next_inspection_candidate(
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        tenant_id: str,
        pos_created: str | None,
        pos_rid: str | None,
    ) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
        """Oldest request strictly after the keyset position.

        Every request of the tenant is swept, whatever its status: the
        inspection covers the settled audit chain each acceptance
        started. The (created_at, request_id) ordering is the same
        stable order the claim and reconcile scans use, so the sweep is
        stable across calls, restarts and concurrent submissions.
        """
        if pos_created is None:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT request_id, created_at FROM requests "
                "WHERE tenant_id = ? "
                "ORDER BY created_at ASC, request_id ASC LIMIT 1",
                (tenant_id,),
            ).fetchone()
        return conn.execute(
            "SELECT request_id, created_at FROM requests "
            "WHERE tenant_id = ? AND (created_at, request_id) > (?, ?) "
            "ORDER BY created_at ASC, request_id ASC LIMIT 1",
            (tenant_id, pos_created, pos_rid),
        ).fetchone()

    @staticmethod
    def _advance_inspection_locked(
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        batch_id: str,
        pos_created: str,
        pos_rid: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Move the inspection batch's durable keyset position forward."""
        cursor = conn.execute(
            "UPDATE inspection_batches "
            "SET position_created_at = ?, position_request_id = ? "
            "WHERE batch_id = ?",
            (pos_created, pos_rid, batch_id),
        )
        if cursor.rowcount != 1:
            # The batch row this transaction itself resolved vanished;
            # that is storage corruption, never a caller error.
            raise _storage_failure()

    @staticmethod
    def _finish_inspection_locked(conn: sqlite3.Connection, batch_id: str) -> None:
        """Mark the inspection batch durably finished in the open txn."""
        cursor = conn.execute(
            "UPDATE inspection_batches SET finished = 1 WHERE batch_id = ?",
            (batch_id,),
        )
        if cursor.rowcount != 1:
            raise _storage_failure()

    def _inspect_request_locked(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        tenant_id: str,
        request_id: str,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Assess one request's settled chain inside the open transaction.

        Reads the same persisted evidence the full-chain assessment
        uses, then evaluates the request's own chain together with the
        file-wide seal that also binds it. Purely read-only: nothing is
        written, repaired, recomputed-into-place or overwritten.
        """
        meta_rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT head_hmac FROM audit_anchor_meta"
        ).fetchall()
        event_rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT tenant_id, request_id, seq, status, occurred_at, "
            "chain_hash FROM status_events ORDER BY tenant_id, request_id, seq"
        ).fetchall()
        anchor_rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT commit_seq, tenant_id, request_id, seq, event_hash, "
            "anchor_hmac, key_generation FROM audit_anchors ORDER BY commit_seq"
        ).fetchall()
        request_rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT tenant_id, request_id, status, chain_hash FROM requests"
        ).fetchall()
        generation_rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT generation, key_fingerprint, effective_at "
            "FROM anchor_key_generations ORDER BY generation"
        ).fetchall()
        reasons = self._evaluate_inspection_rows(
            tuple(meta_rows),
            tuple(event_rows),
            tuple(anchor_rows),
            tuple(request_rows),
            tuple(generation_rows),
            self._anchor_secret,
            self._anchor_history_secrets,
            (tenant_id, request_id),
        )
        return {
            "request_id": request_id,
            "verified": not reasons,
            "reason": reasons[0] if reasons else "",
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _evaluate_inspection_rows(
        meta_rows: tuple,
        event_rows: tuple,
        anchor_rows: tuple,
        request_rows: tuple,
        generation_rows: tuple,
        secret: str | None,
        history_secrets: Mapping[int, str],
        scope: tuple[str, str],
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Pure, read-only per-request evaluation of the persisted chain.

        Kept free of any connection so the logic is deterministic and
        side-effect free: it only compares and recomputes, never writes.
        Returns the sorted stable reason codes that make the scoped
        request's settled audit chain untrusted -- an empty list means
        the request verifies. Two layers are assessed:

        * the request's own evidence: event order and database link
          hashes, the request row's chain head and current status, the
          one-to-one event/anchor binding and every anchor's
          authentication under the secret of the generation recorded on
          its own row;
        * the file-wide seal the request cannot be trusted without: the
          singleton meta head, the secret-generation records, the
          gap-free global commit order, the replayed global anchor head
          and file-wide split or orphaned evidence.
        """
        scope_tenant, scope_request = scope
        global_reasons: set[str] = set()
        scoped_reasons: set[str] = set()

        # -- singleton meta head (file-wide) -------------------------
        stored_head: str | None = None
        if len(meta_rows) > 1:
            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_META_CORRUPT)
        elif meta_rows:
            stored_head = meta_rows[0][0]
            if not _is_chain_hash(stored_head):
                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_META_CORRUPT)
                stored_head = None

        # -- secret generations (file-wide) --------------------------
        # One gap-free row per generation that has ever sealed anchors,
        # starting at 1, each with a well-formed fingerprint and an
        # effective time; legacy anchors carry NULL and are attributed
        # to generation 1.
        generation_fingerprints: dict[int, str] = {}
        generation_corrupt = False
        for index, grow in enumerate(generation_rows, start=1):
            generation, fingerprint, effective_at = grow
            if (
                not isinstance(generation, int)
                or isinstance(generation, bool)
                or generation != index
                or not _is_chain_hash(fingerprint)
                or not isinstance(effective_at, str)
                or not _RFC3339_RE.match(effective_at)
            ):
                generation_corrupt = True
            if isinstance(generation, int) and not isinstance(generation, bool):
                generation_fingerprints[generation] = fingerprint
        if anchor_rows and generation_corrupt:
            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_CORRUPT_ROW)
        if generation_rows and not anchor_rows:
            # Secret generations without a single anchor are only valid
            # as the bootstrap-rotation shape (exactly generations 1 and
            # 2 sharing one effective time).
            bootstrap_shape = (
                not generation_corrupt
                and [g for g, _f, _t in generation_rows] == [1, 2]
                and generation_rows[0][2] == generation_rows[1][2]
            )
            if not bootstrap_shape:
                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_CORRUPT_ROW)

        # -- event/anchor population invariants (file-wide) ----------
        # A database with events but no anchor rows is the historical
        # un-anchored shape: old content is never judged trusted.
        legacy_unanchored = bool(event_rows) and not anchor_rows
        if legacy_unanchored:
            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_UNANCHORED)
        if anchor_rows and not event_rows:
            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_STATE_SPLIT)
        if anchor_rows and stored_head is None:
            # Sealed anchors without a global head: an interrupted
            # commit or out-of-band deletion.
            global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_META_CORRUPT)

        # -- index the rows ------------------------------------------
        # A malformed evidence row anywhere corrupts the file every
        # request's seal is replayed against, so it is a file-wide
        # reason rather than a per-request one.
        events: dict[tuple, tuple] = {}
        for row in event_rows:
            tenant_id, request_id, seq, status, occurred_at, chain_hash = row
            key = (tenant_id, request_id, seq)
            if (
                not isinstance(tenant_id, str)
                or not tenant_id
                or not isinstance(request_id, str)
                or not request_id
                or not isinstance(seq, int)
                or isinstance(seq, bool)
                or not isinstance(status, str)
                or not status
                or not isinstance(occurred_at, str)
                or not occurred_at
                or not _is_chain_hash(chain_hash)
            ):
                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_CORRUPT_ROW)
            if key in events:
                global_reasons.add(_ANCHOR_REASON_CORRUPT_ROW)
            events[key] = row

        anchors: dict[tuple, tuple] = {}
        for row in anchor_rows:
            (
                commit_seq,
                tenant_id,
                request_id,
                seq,
                event_hash,
                anchor_hmac,
                key_generation,
            ) = row
            key = (tenant_id, request_id, seq)
            if (
                not isinstance(commit_seq, int)
                or isinstance(commit_seq, bool)
                or commit_seq < 1
                or not isinstance(tenant_id, str)
                or not tenant_id
                or not isinstance(request_id, str)
                or not request_id
                or not isinstance(seq, int)
                or isinstance(seq, bool)
                or not _is_chain_hash(event_hash)
                or not _is_chain_hash(anchor_hmac)
                # NULL is the legacy attribution (generation 1); any
                # present value must be a positive integer.
                or not (
                    key_generation is None

def reconcile_batch(
        self,
        tenant_id: str,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        limit: int | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Reconcile a tenant's pending requests in resumable batches.

        Storage-layer only; never routed over HTTP. With ``cursor``
        omitted a new persistent batch sweeps the tenant's requests in
        stable acceptance order (``created_at`` then ``request_id``);
        with a cursor the batch it names is resumed from its durably
        committed position, so a retry after an interruption continues
        instead of restarting, and the same cursor always keeps the same
        batch identifier. Each call reconciles at most ``limit`` items
        (default 100, at most 1000) and returns exactly ``batch_id``,
        ``next_cursor`` (``None`` once the sweep is finished),
        ``finished`` and ``items`` -- one ``{"request_id", "status"}``
        entry per reconciled request, in scan order.

        Reconciliation of each request follows
        :meth:`reconcile_execution`: ``accepted`` rows are skipped
        without creating an attempt, receipt or extra status event;
        a ``processing`` request with a live lease stays processing; a
        ``processing`` request whose lease expired (or that has no
        explainable lease) is compensated to ``failed``. Every item's
        status change, attempt rows, lease release, batch bookkeeping
        and cursor position commit in one transaction, so a failed call
        leaves no half-settled item and a committed item is never
        rewritten by a retry.

        A non-string/empty *tenant_id*, a limit outside 1..1000 (or a
        non-integer), and any malformed, unknown or cross-tenant
        *cursor* raise :class:`ValueError` without writing. Corrupt
        persisted batch state and every storage fault raise the
        fixed-text :class:`OSError`.
        """
        # Validate everything before touching the database: no rejected
        # call may perform a write.
        tenant_id = _require_nonempty_str(tenant_id, "tenant_id")
        if limit is None:
            limit = _DEFAULT_BATCH_LIMIT
        limit = _require_batch_limit(limit)
        cursor_batch: tuple[str, int] | None = None
        if cursor is not None:
            cursor_batch = _decode_cursor(cursor)

        with self._write_lock:
            conn = self._connect()
            try:
                # First transaction resolves the batch: a fresh batch row
                # is inserted when no cursor was given; a cursor names the
                # persisted batch to resume. An unknown/cross-tenant cursor
                # is rejected here before anything is written.
                batch_id, _pos, _rid, finished, _start_count = (
                    self._batch_transaction(
                        conn,
                        lambda: self._load_or_init_batch_locked(
                            conn, tenant_id, cursor_batch
                        ),
                    )
                )
                items: list[dict[str, str]] = []
                # Each scanned request is settled in its OWN transaction:
                # its status change, attempts, lease release, the item row
                # and the cursor position all commit together. The next
                # iteration re-reads the persisted position, so an item
                # already settled by an earlier commit or a concurrent call
                # is never rewritten.
                while not finished and len(items) < limit:
                    kind, payload = self._batch_transaction(
                        conn,
                        lambda: self._process_one_batch_item_locked(
                            conn, tenant_id, batch_id
                        ),
                    )
                    if kind == "finished":
                        finished = True
                        break
                    if kind == "item":
                        items.append(payload)
                    # "accepted" only advanced the position and is skipped.
                # Resolve the authoritative outcome in one final short
                # transaction: whether the sweep is finished AND the durable
                # settled-item count are both read from the database rather
                # than from this call's in-memory tally. A file database may
                # be shared by other RequestStore instances/processes whose
                # per-item transactions commit disjoint items for the same
                # resumable batch; the cursor's position must name that
                # durable count, never a stale "start + this call's items"
                # snapshot that lags behind what is already settled.
                finished, durable_count = self._batch_transaction(
                    conn,
                    lambda: self._finalize_batch_if_end_locked(
                        conn, tenant_id, batch_id
                    ),
                )
            finally:
                self._release(conn)
        # The cursor only identifies the persisted batch; its item count is
        # the database-authoritative settled count read in the final
        # transaction, so a cursor returned to any concurrent caller reports
        # a position that matches what is durably committed.
        next_cursor = (
            None if finished else _encode_cursor(batch_id, durable_count)
        )
        # Log only counts and the stable outcome: no tenant, subject,
        # worker, credential or SQL text ever reaches the log.
        _log.info(
            "reconcile batch settled items=%s finished=%s",
            len(items),
            finished,
        )
        return {
            "batch_id": batch_id,
            "next_cursor": next_cursor,
            "finished": finished,
            "items": items,
        }

    def _batch_transaction(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, action):
        """Run ``action`` inside one short-lived write transaction.

        Every batch operation (batch resolution, one item, the end
        finalization) commits independently, so a fault while settling a
        later item can never undo an already committed earlier item or
        leave the shared connection inside an aborted transaction. Domain
        and storage exceptions propagate after a rollback; any engine
        error -- including lock conflicts -- becomes the fixed-text
        :class:`OSError`.
        """
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        except sqlite3.Error:
            raise _storage_failure() from None
        try:
            result = action()
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
            return result
        except ValueError:
            self._rollback_quietly(conn)
            raise
        except (RequestNotFound, InvalidStatusTransition):
            # Defensive only: rows are read inside this write transaction
            # and cannot vanish or move illegally underneath it.
            self._rollback_quietly(conn)
            raise _storage_failure() from None
        except OSError:
            self._rollback_quietly(conn)
            raise
        except sqlite3.Error:
            self._rollback_quietly(conn)
            raise _storage_failure() from None

    @staticmethod
    def _rollback_quietly(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        try:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        except sqlite3.Error:
            pass

"""Tests for read-only, resumable batch audit inspection.

Covers RequestStore.audit_inspection on the storage layer only: the
fixed result shape, stable acceptance-order scanning, per-item verified
flag and stable reason codes, tamper detection (event delete/alter/
insert/reorder, cross-request and cross-tenant substitution, chain
head, anchor and global head corruption), legacy un-anchored and
secret-missing databases, historical-secret rotation handling, cursor
pagination and resume across rebuilds, validation without writes,
corruption semantics and the strict read-only guarantee for every
audit, anchor and key record. This entry point is deliberately not
exposed over HTTP.
"""

import os
import sqlite3
import tempfile
import unittest

from forgetting_evidence.requests import (
    RequestStore,
    _INSPECTION_CURSOR_PREFIX,
    _encode_cursor,
)


class _StoreCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self._tmp.name, "nested", "evidence.db")

    def tearDown(self):
        self._tmp.cleanup()

    def _store(self, secret="anchor-secret", history=None):
        return RequestStore(
            self.db_path, anchor_secret=secret, anchor_history_secrets=history
        )

    def _submit_many(self, store, count, tenant="tenant-a"):
        return [
            store.submit(tenant, f"subject-{i}", ["email"], f"key-{i}")["request_id"]
            for i in range(count)
        ]

    def _raw(self):
        return sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)

    def _table_dump(self, table):
        with self._raw() as raw:
            return raw.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table}").fetchall()


class InspectionShapeTests(_StoreCase):
    def test_empty_tenant_finishes_with_no_items(self):
        store = self._store()
        result = store.audit_inspection("tenant-a")
        self.assertEqual(
            list(result), ["batch_id", "next_cursor", "finished", "items"]
        )
        self.assertIsInstance(result["batch_id"], str)
        self.assertTrue(result["batch_id"])
        self.assertIsNone(result["next_cursor"])
        self.assertIs(result["finished"], True)
        self.assertEqual(result["items"], [])

    def test_healthy_requests_verify_with_empty_reason(self):
        store = self._store()
        request_ids = self._submit_many(store, 3)
        result = store.audit_inspection("tenant-a")
        self.assertIs(result["finished"], True)
        self.assertEqual([item["request_id"] for item in result["items"]], request_ids)
        for item in result["items"]:
            self.assertEqual(set(item), {"request_id", "verified", "reason"})
            self.assertIs(item["verified"], True)
            self.assertEqual(item["reason"], "")

5049	        acceptance time, the final completion time, a scope commitment
5050	        digest and a completing-attempt digest, plus an authentication
5051	        tag computed under the caller-held *key*. Only a request whose
5052	        deletion completed with a settled execution record -- the
5053	        earliest terminal attempt recorded ``completed`` -- can be
5054	        issued a receipt; an accepted, processing or failed request (or
5055	        a completed status without a completed terminal attempt) raises
5056	        :class:`ReceiptUnavailable`.

5059	        no status, attempt, lease or audit record is created or altered.

5061	        whichever key is presented, and concurrent generations persist
5062	        exactly one record. A corrupt stored receipt raises the
5063	        fixed-text :class:`OSError`; it is never repaired, recomputed or
5064	        overwritten. The key is never persisted, returned or logged.

5067	        :class:`ValueError` without writing; a missing, empty,

5069	        never-accepted *request_id* raises :class:`RequestNotFound`

5071	        which ids exist.

5076	        with :class:`ReceiptKeyConflict` -- an old key can never mint a

5088	        key = _require_nonempty_str(key, "key")

5091	            conn = self._connect()
5092	            try:
5093	                try:
5094	                    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
5095	                except sqlite3.Error:
5096	                    raise _storage_failure() from None

5098	                    text = self._generate_receipt_locked(
5099	                        conn, tenant_id, request_id, key
5100	                    )
5101	                    conn.execute("COMMIT")

5103	                    self._rollback_quietly(conn)

5105	                except OSError:

5107	                    raise
5108	                except sqlite3.IntegrityError:

5110	                    # creators in this process; the unique keys can
5111	                    # only fire if another process sharing the file
5112	                    # committed first. Resolve which race this was:
5113	                    # the same receipt was generated first (replay its
5114	                    # stored bytes, whichever key we presented), or the
5115	                    # tenant's generation 1 was registered by another
5116	                    # first mint with a different active key (a key
5117	                    # conflict; never mint under a non-active key).

5120	                        conn, tenant_id, request_id, key
5121	                    )
5122	                except sqlite3.Error:
5123	                    self._rollback_quietly(conn)
5124	                    raise _storage_failure() from None

5126	                self._release(conn)

5130	    def _resolve_lost_mint_race(
5131	        self,
5132	        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
5133	        tenant_id: str,
5134	        request_id: str,
5135	        key: str,
5136	    ) -> str:
5137	        """Re-evaluate a mint after another process won a unique-key race.
5138	
5139	        A fresh write transaction re-runs the whole decision: the
5140	        receipt may now exist (its stored first bytes are replayed no
5141	        matter which key is presented), the tenant's generation 1 may
5142	        now be registered with a matching active key (the mint
5143	        proceeds under it), or the active key may be a different one
5144	        (the detail-free :class:`ReceiptKeyConflict` stands; a retired
5145	        or foreign key never mints).
5146	        """
5147	        try:
5148	            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
5149	            text = self._generate_receipt_locked(conn, tenant_id, request_id, key)
5150	            conn.execute("COMMIT")
5151	            return text
5152	        except (RequestNotFound, ReceiptUnavailable, ReceiptKeyConflict):
5153	            self._rollback_quietly(conn)
5154	            raise
5155	        except OSError:
5156	            self._rollback_quietly(conn)
5157	            raise
5158	        except sqlite3.Error:
5159	            self._rollback_quietly(conn)

5162	    def _generate_receipt_locked(
5163	        self,
5164	        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
5165	        tenant_id: str,
5166	        request_id: str,
5167	        key: str,
5168	    ) -> str:
5169	        """Issue or replay the receipt inside an open write txn."""
5170	        row = conn.execute(
5171	            "SELECT status, created_at, scopes_json FROM requests "
5172	            "WHERE tenant_id = ? AND request_id = ?",
5173	            (tenant_id, request_id),
5174	        ).fetchone()
5175	        if row is None:
5176	            # Unknown, cross-tenant and never-accepted ids share one
5177	            # outcome, so the call cannot reveal which records exist.
5178	            raise RequestNotFound("request not found")
5179	        status, created_at, scopes_json = row
5180	
5181	        stored = self._load_receipt_row_locked(conn, tenant_id, request_id)
5182	        if stored is not None:
5183	            # Idempotent replay: the first receipt is returned exactly
5184	            # as stored, whichever key is presented now. It is never
5185	            # recomputed, backfilled or overwritten.
5186	            return stored[1]
5187	
5188	        if (
5189	            status not in _ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS
5190	            or not isinstance(created_at, str)
5191	            or not created_at
5192	        ):
5193	            # A status outside the lifecycle or a broken acceptance time
5194	            # is out-of-band corruption, never a receiptable state.
5195	            raise _storage_failure()
5196	        if status != _STATUS_COMPLETED:
5197	            # Accepted, processing and failed requests cannot obtain a
5198	            # deletion receipt; the fixed message does not say which.
5199	            raise ReceiptUnavailable(_RECEIPT_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE)
5200	
5201	        try:
5202	            scopes = json.loads(scopes_json)
5203	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
5204	            raise _storage_failure() from None
5205	        if (
5206	            not isinstance(scopes, list)
5207	            or not scopes
5208	            or not all(isinstance(item, str) and item for item in scopes)
5209	        ):
5210	            raise _storage_failure()
5211	
5212	        attempts = self._load_attempts_for_receipt(conn, tenant_id, request_id)
5213	        terminals = [
5214	            attempt for attempt in attempts if attempt["result"] is not None
5215	        ]
5216	        if not terminals:
5217	            # A completed status without any settled execution record
5218	            # (e.g. a bare status-machine transition) has no completed
5219	            # deletion to attest.
5220	            raise ReceiptUnavailable(_RECEIPT_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE)
5221	        # The earliest completion wins; later duplicate terminal rows
5222	        # never alter the receipt's content.
5223	        earliest = min(
5224	            terminals,
5225	            key=lambda attempt: (
5226	                attempt["completed_at"],  # type: ignore[index]
5227	                attempt["attempt_number"],
5228	            ),
5229	        )
5230	        if earliest["result"] != _STATUS_COMPLETED:
5231	            # The settled execution record does not show a completed
5232	            # deletion, so no deletion receipt may be issued.
5233	            raise ReceiptUnavailable(_RECEIPT_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE)
5234	
5235	        fields: dict[str, str] = {
5236	            "tenant_id": tenant_id,
5237	            "request_id": request_id,
5238	            "created_at": created_at,
5239	            "completed_at": earliest["completed_at"],  # type: ignore[assignment]
5240	            "scope_digest": _scope_digest(tenant_id, request_id, scopes),
5241	            "attempt_digest": _attempt_digest(tenant_id, request_id, earliest),
5242	        }
5243	        # Mint only under the tenant's current active key. The first
5244	        # receipt a tenant ever issues registers its presented key as
5245	        # generation 1 in the same transaction as the receipt row, so
5246	        # the two can never disagree (and a rollback never leaves a
5247	        # key generation without the receipt that introduced it).
5248	        # After a rotation the active key is the only key allowed to
5249	        # sign a new receipt: a retired key reaching this mint path
5250	        # without a stored receipt is rejected without writing.
5251	        self._require_active_or_bootstrap_key_locked(conn, tenant_id, key)

5253	        text = _render_receipt(fields)
5254	        # The receipt row is the only write of this transaction; it
5255	        # commits atomically and never half-exists.
5256	        conn.execute(
5257	            "INSERT INTO deletion_receipts (tenant_id, request_id, receipt_json) "
5258	            "VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
5259	            (tenant_id, request_id, text),
5260	        )
5261	        return text

5263	    @staticmethod
5264	    def _load_receipt_row_locked(
5265	        conn: sqlite3.Connection, tenant_id: str, request_id: str
5266	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, str], str] | None:
5267	        """Return ``(fields, text)`` of the persisted receipt, or None.
5268	
5269	        The stored text must parse as a well-formed receipt and be
5270	        exactly the canonical rendering of its fields. Anything else is
5271	        out-of-band corruption and raises the fixed-text
5272	        :class:`OSError`; the record is never repaired, recomputed or
5273	        overwritten on the way out.
5274	        """
5275	        row = conn.execute(
5276	            "SELECT receipt_json FROM deletion_receipts "
5277	            "WHERE tenant_id = ? AND request_id = ?",
5278	            (tenant_id, request_id),
5279	        ).fetchone()
5280	        if row is None:
5281	            return None
5282	        text = row[0]
5283	        if not isinstance(text, str):
5284	            raise _storage_failure()
5285	        try:
5286	            fields = _parse_receipt_text(text)
5287	        except ValueError:
5288	            raise _storage_failure() from None
5289	        if _render_receipt(fields) != text:
5290	            # Only the canonical rendering is ever written; a
5291	            # re-serialised or reordered record was altered out of band.
5292	            raise _storage_failure()

5295	    @staticmethod
5296	    def _load_attempts_for_receipt(
5297	        conn: sqlite3.Connection, tenant_id: str, request_id: str
5298	    ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
5299	        """Read and strictly validate every attempt row for a receipt.
5300	
5301	        A malformed sequence, timestamp or result/completion pairing is
5302	        storage corruption and raises the fixed-text :class:`OSError`
5303	        before any receipt is built from the rows.
5304	        """
5305	        rows = conn.execute(
5306	            "SELECT attempt_number, claimed_at, lease_expires_at, "
5307	            "result, completed_at FROM claim_attempts "
5308	            "WHERE tenant_id = ? AND request_id = ? ORDER BY attempt_number",
5309	            (tenant_id, request_id),
5310	        ).fetchall()
5311	        attempts: list[dict[str, object]] = []
5312	        for index, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
5313	            attempt_number, claimed_at, lease_expires_at, result, completed_at = row
5314	            if (
5315	                not isinstance(attempt_number, int)
5316	                or isinstance(attempt_number, bool)
5317	                or attempt_number != index
5318	                or not isinstance(claimed_at, str)
5319	                or not claimed_at
5320	                or not isinstance(lease_expires_at, str)
5321	                or not lease_expires_at
5322	            ):
5323	                raise _storage_failure()
5324	            if result is not None and (
5325	                not isinstance(result, str) or result not in _TERMINAL_RESULTS
5326	            ):
5327	                raise _storage_failure()
5328	            if completed_at is not None and (
5329	                not isinstance(completed_at, str) or not completed_at
5330	            ):
5331	                raise _storage_failure()
5332	            # Result and completion time are set together and never
5333	            # separately; a split row is a broken invariant.
5334	            if (result is None) != (completed_at is None):
5335	                raise _storage_failure()
5336	            attempts.append(
5337	                {
5338	                    "attempt_number": attempt_number,
5339	                    "claimed_at": claimed_at,
5340	                    "lease_expires_at": lease_expires_at,
5341	                    "result": result,
5342	                    "completed_at": completed_at,
5343	                }
5344	            )
5345	        return attempts

5349	    @staticmethod
5350	    def _load_key_generations_locked(
5351	        conn: sqlite3.Connection, tenant_id: str
5352	    ) -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]:
5353	        """Return a tenant's registered key generations as strict rows.
5354	
5355	        Rows are ``(generation, fingerprint, effective_at)`` in
5356	        generation order. Generations start at 1 and are gap-free, each
5357	        fingerprint is 64 lowercase hex characters and each effective
5358	        time a UTC RFC3339 string; anything else is out-of-band
5359	        corruption and raises the fixed-text :class:`OSError`, never a
5360	        half-read generation set.
5361	        """
5362	        rows = conn.execute(
5363	            "SELECT generation, key_fingerprint, effective_at "
5364	            "FROM receipt_keys WHERE tenant_id = ? ORDER BY generation",
5365	            (tenant_id,),
5366	        ).fetchall()
5367	        generations: list[tuple[int, str, str]] = []
5368	        for index, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
5369	            generation, fingerprint, effective_at = row
5370	            if (
5371	                not isinstance(generation, int)
5372	                or isinstance(generation, bool)
5373	                or generation != index
5374	                or not _is_chain_hash(fingerprint)
5375	                or not isinstance(effective_at, str)
5376	                or not _RFC3339_RE.match(effective_at)
5377	            ):
5378	                raise _storage_failure()
5379	            generations.append((generation, fingerprint, effective_at))
5380	        return generations

5382	    def _require_active_or_bootstrap_key_locked(
5383	        self,
5384	        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
5385	        tenant_id: str,
5386	        key: str,
5387	    ) -> None:
5388	        """Admit *key* as the minting key inside an open write txn.
5389	
5390	        A tenant's first ever receipt bootstraps generation 1 with the
5391	        presented key, inserted in the same transaction as the receipt
5392	        row. Afterwards only the current active generation may sign a
5393	        new receipt: a retired or never-registered key reaches the mint
5394	        path without a stored receipt and gets the single, detail-free
5395	        :class:`ReceiptKeyConflict`, so which fingerprints exist can
5396	        never be probed through distinct failures.
5397	
5398	        The full generation set is validated (gap-free generations with
5399	        well-formed fingerprints and times) before the active row is
5400	        trusted: a tampered key history is storage corruption and
5401	        raises the fixed-text :class:`OSError` rather than minting off
5402	        a forged active row.
5403	        """
5404	        generations = self._load_key_generations_locked(conn, tenant_id)
5405	        fingerprint = _key_fingerprint(key)
5406	        if not generations:
5407	            conn.execute(
5408	                "INSERT INTO receipt_keys ("
5409	                "tenant_id, generation, key_fingerprint, effective_at"
5410	                ") VALUES (?, 1, ?, ?)",
5411	                (tenant_id, fingerprint, _utc_now_rfc3339()),
5412	            )
5413	            return
5414	        active_fingerprint = generations[-1][1]
5415	        if not hmac.compare_digest(active_fingerprint, fingerprint):
5416	            raise ReceiptKeyConflict(_RECEIPT_KEY_CONFLICT_MESSAGE)

5418	    def rotate_receipt_key(
5419	        self,
5420	        tenant_id: str,
5421	        retired_key: str,
5422	        new_key: str,
5423	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
5424	        """Rotate the tenant's receipt authentication key.
5425	
5426	        Storage-layer only; never routed over HTTP. *retired_key* is
5427	        the tenant's currently active key and *new_key* its successor.
5428	        On success exactly one new generation becomes active and the
5429	        result carries ``generation`` (a positive int) and
5430	        ``effective_at`` (the UTC RFC3339 rotation time); old
5431	        generations remain registered solely so receipts signed under
5432	        them keep verifying, and only fingerprints, generations and
5433	        times are persisted -- key material never enters the database,
5434	        a return value, an exception or a log.
5435	
5436	        * With no generation registered yet (no receipt was ever
5437	          generated) the first rotation establishes generations 1 and
5438	          2 atomically and returns generation 2.
5439	        * Repeating the rotation that produced the active generation is
5440	          idempotent and returns that first generation and its first
5441	          effective time.
5442	        * A retired key that is registered but no longer active, the
5443	          replay of an already superseded rotation pair, or a successor
5444	          key already registered raises :class:`ReceiptKeyConflict`
5445	          with generations unchanged; a concurrent rotation with a
5446	          different successor loses identically, so only the first
5447	          transaction ever produces the active generation.
5448	        * When generations already exist but *retired_key* names no
5449	          registered generation, :class:`ValueError` is raised; empty
5450	          or non-string arguments and identical keys are
5451	          :class:`ValueError` as well, and no rejected call commits.
5452	
5453	        Generations, times and historical receipts survive restarts;
5454	        an unfinished rotation is rolled back as a whole and can never
5455	        appear effective. Every storage fault is the fixed-text
5456	        :class:`OSError`.
5457	        """
5458	        tenant_id = _require_nonempty_str(tenant_id, "tenant_id")
5459	        retired_key = _require_nonempty_str(retired_key, "retired_key")
5460	        new_key = _require_nonempty_str(new_key, "new_key")
5461	        if retired_key == new_key:
5462	            raise ValueError("retired_key and new_key must differ")
5463	
5464	        with self._write_lock:
5465	            conn = self._connect()
5466	            try:
5467	                try:
5468	                    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
5469	                except sqlite3.Error:
5470	                    raise _storage_failure() from None
5471	                try:
5472	                    result = self._rotate_receipt_key_locked(
5473	                        conn, tenant_id, retired_key, new_key
5474	                    )
5475	                    conn.execute("COMMIT")
5476	                except (ValueError, ReceiptKeyConflict):
5477	                    self._rollback_quietly(conn)
5478	                    raise
5479	                except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
5480	                    # Another process sharing the file won the same
5481	                    # generation slot: an identical rotation replays
5482	                    # idempotently, any other lost race is a conflict.
5483	                    self._rollback_quietly(conn)
5484	                    result = self._resolve_lost_rotation_race(
5485	                        conn, tenant_id, retired_key, new_key
5486	                    )
5487	                except sqlite3.Error:
5488	                    self._rollback_quietly(conn)
5489	                    raise _storage_failure() from None
5490	            finally:
5491	                self._release(conn)
5492	        # Only the generation number is logged -- never a fingerprint
5493	        # or any key material.
5494	        _log.info("receipt key rotated generation=%s", result["generation"])
5495	        return result

5497	    def _rotate_receipt_key_locked(
5498	        self,
5499	        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
5500	        tenant_id: str,
5501	        retired_key: str,
5502	        new_key: str,
5503	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
5504	        """Apply one rotation inside an already-open write transaction."""
5505	        generations = self._load_key_generations_locked(conn, tenant_id)
5506	        retired_fp = _key_fingerprint(retired_key)
5507	        new_fp = _key_fingerprint(new_key)
5508	
5509	        if not generations:
5510	            # No active generation yet: the first rotation establishes
5511	            # both generation 1 (the retired key) and generation 2 (the
5512	            # new key) in this one atomic commit. Receipts generated
5513	            # afterwards are signed by generation 2; receipts that were
5514	            # minted before any rotation cannot exist for this tenant.
5515	            effective_at = _utc_now_rfc3339()
5516	            conn.execute(
5517	                "INSERT INTO receipt_keys ("
5518	                "tenant_id, generation, key_fingerprint, effective_at"
5519	                ") VALUES (?, 1, ?, ?), (?, 2, ?, ?)",
5520	                (
5521	                    tenant_id,
5522	                    retired_fp,
5523	                    effective_at,
5524	                    tenant_id,
5525	                    new_fp,
5526	                    effective_at,
5527	                ),
5528	            )
5529	            return {"generation": 2, "effective_at": effective_at}
5530	
5531	        active_generation, active_fp, active_effective_at = generations[-1]
5532	
5533	        # Idempotent replay first: the exact pair that produced the
5534	        # active generation returns the first generation and time, even
5535	        # though the retired key is no longer current.
5536	        if len(generations) >= 2:
5537	            predecessor_fp = generations[-2][1]
5538	            if hmac.compare_digest(
5539	                predecessor_fp, retired_fp
5540	            ) and hmac.compare_digest(active_fp, new_fp):
5541	                return {
5542	                    "generation": active_generation,
5543	                    "effective_at": active_effective_at,
5544	                }
5545	
5546	        if hmac.compare_digest(retired_fp, active_fp):
5547	            for _gen, fingerprint, _at in generations:
5548	                if hmac.compare_digest(fingerprint, new_fp):
5549	                    # The successor already has a generation (a retired
5550	                    # key, or the active key itself); reusing it would
5551	                    # alias generations and is rejected unchanged.
5552	                    raise ReceiptKeyConflict(_RECEIPT_KEY_CONFLICT_MESSAGE)

5554	            conn.execute(
5555	                "INSERT INTO receipt_keys ("
5556	                "tenant_id, generation, key_fingerprint, effective_at"
5557	                ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
5558	                (tenant_id, active_generation + 1, new_fp, effective_at),
5559	            )
5560	            return {
5561	                "generation": active_generation + 1,
5562	                "effective_at": effective_at,
5563	            }
5564	
5565	        # The retired key is not the active generation. A consecutive
5566	        # historical pair presented again after it was superseded is
5567	        # the explicit "superseded rotation combination" conflict; any
5568	        # other registered-but-old key simply does not match the
5569	        # current generation. Both share one detail-free outcome.
5570	        for index in range(len(generations) - 1):
5571	            if hmac.compare_digest(
5572	                generations[index][1], retired_fp
5573	            ) and hmac.compare_digest(generations[index + 1][1], new_fp):
5574	                raise ReceiptKeyConflict(_RECEIPT_KEY_CONFLICT_MESSAGE)
5575	        if any(
5576	            hmac.compare_digest(fingerprint, retired_fp)
5577	            for _gen, fingerprint, _at in generations
5578	        ):
5579	            raise ReceiptKeyConflict(_RECEIPT_KEY_CONFLICT_MESSAGE)

5581	        # of them: the rotation is missing the generation it claims to
5582	        # retire. Caller error, not a conflict -- and nothing commits.
5583	        raise ValueError("retired_key does not name a registered generation")

5585	    def _resolve_lost_rotation_race(
